newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah wavers amid flush liquidity.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah wavers amid flush liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah came under further pressure amid flush money market liquidity on Wednesday, dealers said.

A U.S. bank dealer in Jakarta said there were some selling orders at the 2,380.0 level and continued short-covering by Singapore players pushed the rupiah to breach the support level and fall to a low of 2,384.0 in mid-morning.
"But the market has consolidated a bit. Local profit-taking seems to have helped limit rupiah declines," the dealer said.
One European bank dealer said maturing dollar call options seemed to have triggered dollar short-covering.
He said call options with strike prices around the 2,380 and 2,385 levels were due, leading investors to exercise the options.
"There is still some upward potential for dollars to rise if the options were exercised, coupled with ample rupiah supply and a tight dollar market," the dealer said.
However, he added the condition could be different if heavy dollar selling occurred in the market.
"The tone is still biddish for the dollar," he said.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,378.00/79.00 at 0445 GMT against its opening 2,377.0/80.0.
Dealers said short-dated swap rates remained under pressure as short dollar operators were further squeezed on the back of sustained ample rupiah liquidity in the money market.
"The tom/next market is still very flush with liquidity so being long dollars is more profitable than being short," said a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore.
He said the dollar would face some temporary resistance around 2,383/85 but added that it looked well supported at the base as the market was still quite short of dollars.
In Malaysia, the ringgit had a choppy morning as fresh bids emerged after the dollar failed to breach resistance around 2.4850/60, dealers said.
"The market tried to push the dollar above 2.4850 yesterday and today, but it seems there's not enough momentum at the moment," said the U.S. bank dealer.
He said the ringgit was likely to trade within a 2.4770-2.4850 range against the dollar for the time being.
"The ringgit is consolidating after the recent run up. But there is a lot of dollar selling at the present levels," said a dealer with another U.S. bank in Singapore.
She said there was also demand for the dollar from Kuala Lumpur, which could offset some of the Malaysian currency's potential gains.
Across the border, the Singapore dollar slipped a few notches as interbank players bought U.S. dollars against the backdrop of a firmer dollar/mark and dollar/yen.
But dealers said there was selling interest in dollar/Sing around the 1.4065/75 levels.
The Thai baht softened in line with the dollar's firmer tone against the majors, but dealers said it was trading below the central bank's mid-rate, suggesting continuing demand for the Thai currency.
The baht was quoted at 25.673-25.676 to the dollar at 0445 GMT from 25.635-25.645 late on Tuesday. The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.69 against 25.66 on Tuesday.

Dealers said the market showed little reaction to Tuesday's comments by the Bank of Thailand governor and the Thai finance minister, who said separately that Thailand had no plans to devalue the baht and would wait for Thai money markets to stabilise before changing the fixing policy for the baht.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
